County websites not on a .gov domain

1,090 of 2,421 fully scanned U.S. county government websites are not on a .gov domain. A map, the share in each state, and every site listed, from ScanGov homepage scans.

  • Sites: 2821
  • Last scan: 10/3/2026

Of the 2,421 fully scanned U.S. county sites we tested, 1,090 (45%) are not on a .gov domain. Among states with at least 10 tested sites, Oklahoma has the highest share at 88% and Nebraska the lowest at 0%. The check behind this page, Sponsored top-level domain (sTLD), passes when the site uses a government-issued domain (.gov, .edu, or .mil).

About this check

Sponsored top-level domain (sTLD) is one of the security checks. The site uses a government-issued domain (.gov, .edu, or .mil).

Why it matters

Defines trusted website categories, helping users identify official sites and improving credibility and security for specific organizations.

Risk

People cannot tell if your site is real government.

Guidance

  • Sponsored top-level domain (sTLD) standard, with how to fix it
  • U.S. Federal Website Standards
  • Counties security rankings

About this data

ScanGov scans the homepage of each county government site on our county list. Scores come from the checks listed on standards.scangov.org. Sites were scanned between 7/18/2026 and 10/3/2026; each site's report shows its own scan date. A site counts as fully scanned when its homepage returned successfully and sent the scanner its page content. Averages, grade shares, failure rates, and ranks use fully scanned sites only. We weren't able to fully scan 400 sites because they did not respond, blocked the scanner, or returned no page content. They appear in the table without grades, each with its scan status, and are left out of every figure. Grades follow the ScanGov grade scale, and rank follows the ScanGov ranking method. The full dataset, including every county's raw results, is published in the ScanGov data repository.
